identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a single propane-powered forklift (Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2) at Cascade's Portland warehouse, covering September 2026. The log records daily pre-shift safety checks against 12 items required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), with operator initials and notes on defects or maintenance. It is a record of compliance with a federal safety requirement, not itself a regulated document.
scan.freshness_note: The log covers September 2026 and ends 2026-09-19. The supervisor review line is blank and unsigned, and the log is not yet closed for the month. As of today (2026-09-25), this log is current but incomplete—inspections should continue through the end of September and the log should be signed off by a supervisor.

gaps.title: Missing inspections on weekdays Sep 3–4 and Sep 6–7
gaps.description: The hour meter reads 4,819 on Sep 2 and 4,834 on Sep 5, confirming the truck operated on Sep 3–4 (at least 15 hours of runtime). No inspection entries exist for those dates, yet the truck was in use. The same pattern repeats: Sep 6–7 are blank but the truck was running. OSHA requires inspection 'before being placed in service' on each shift the truck is used.
gaps.fix: Retroactively document inspections for Sep 3–4 and Sep 6–7 with the operator's sign-off and any defects noted at the time, or explain in writing why inspections could not be recorded. Add a note to the log explaining the gap. Going forward, ensure inspections are logged on every day the truck is used, regardless of whether the day is a calendar working day.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'Industrial trucks shall be examined before being placed in service...Such examination shall be made at least daily.' The regulation requires daily examination, and the hour meter evidence shows daily operation.
gaps.locator: page 1, rows for Sep 1–2 and Sep 5; page 2 final note confirming runtime on missing dates
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 5 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Defect on Sep 9 (horn not working) — no evidence of removal from service or repair
gaps.description: On Sep 9, the operator marked the horn as defective (X) and noted 'Horn not working' in the Notes column. However, the truck was placed back in service on Sep 10 with a checkmark indicating the horn passed. The log does not show when the horn was repaired, by whom, or that the truck was taken out of service on Sep 9 after the defect was found. OSHA requires defects 'adversely affecting safety' to be reported and corrected immediately, and the truck must not be placed in service if unsafe.
gaps.fix: Add a line or note explaining: (a) what time on Sep 9 the horn defect was identified; (b) when and by whom the horn was repaired; (c) when the truck was re-inspected and cleared for service on Sep 10. Alternatively, if the truck continued in use on Sep 9 after the morning inspection, add a note stating whether the horn was repaired before end-of-shift or before Sep 10 use began. Document the repair work order or maintenance record tied to this log entry.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'shall not be placed in service if the examination shows any condition adversely affecting the safety of the vehicle. Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected.' A non-functional horn is a safety defect (communication with ground personnel).
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 row, 'Horn' column and 'Notes' column
gaps.quote: Sep 9 Day 4,847 ... X ... M.C. Horn not working

gaps.title: Supervisor review signature and date not completed
gaps.description: The form includes a line for 'Supervisor review: ____________________ Date: __________' with both fields blank. OSHA does not explicitly mandate supervisory sign-off on the form itself, but industry best practice and many state/local rules require a supervisor to review the log monthly or at shift end to ensure inspections are being done and defects are being addressed. Without sign-off, there is no clear verification that inspections are being monitored.
gaps.fix: Have the responsible supervisor or safety manager review the entire month's log, verify all entries and notes, and sign and date the form upon completion. Consider establishing a policy that the log is reviewed and signed off by the 5th business day of the following month, or at the end of each week.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) does not explicitly require supervisory signature, but 29 CFR 1910.178(q) broadly requires that defects be 'immediately reported' — a supervisor sign-off helps prove that happened. Oregon OSHA may have additional record-keeping requirements; confirm with Oregon OSHA.

conditions.title: Inspect the forklift before each shift it is placed in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Daily log entries showing the date, shift, operator name, hour-meter reading, and a checkmark or defect mark for each of the 12 items on the checklist (tires, forks, mast, horn, lights, seat belt, brakes, steering, LPG tank, fire extinguisher, data plate, overhead guard). Any defect must be noted with an 'X' and details in the Notes column.

conditions.title: Do not place the truck in service if any condition adversely affects safety
conditions.evidence_expected: A defect entry (X) must be followed by immediate reporting to a supervisor and removal from service. The log should show no subsequent checkmarks for that truck until a repair is documented and a follow-up inspection confirms the defect is corrected.

conditions.title: Defects must be immediately reported and corrected
conditions.evidence_expected: Maintenance work orders, repair invoices, or notes in the 'Notes' column showing what was repaired and when. A follow-up inspection must be logged before the truck returns to service.

conditions.title: Only certified operators may perform inspections
conditions.evidence_expected: Operator certifications showing completion of training and evaluation, with certification dates and expiration dates. The log lists M.C. (certified 2024-03-11, due 2027-03-11) and J.R. (certified 2025-06-02, due 2028-06-02)—both are currently in date.

facts.affects: This is a single vehicle log. If the company operates other forklifts, separate logs are needed for each unit.

facts.quote: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.
facts.affects: The company is required to conduct and log an inspection every day this truck is in use, regardless of day of week. Missing entries are non-compliance with federal OSHA.
